title: A Global Atlas of Digital Dermatology to Map Innovation and Disparities

bias_targets.methodology: Imputing Fitzpatrick skin types for over 1.1 million dermatology images using a multi-modal embedding space and comparing the dataset's distribution against global clinical prevalence to quantify the underrepresentation of darker skin tones.

Analyzing the geographic origin of public dermatology datasets and comparing it to global population distributions to identify the disproportionate overrepresentation of the Global North and the neglect of the Global South.
Imputing patient age across the aggregated dataset and comparing the distribution to global demographics to measure the severe underrepresentation of pediatric populations.
Imputing patient gender and analyzing its overall distribution, as well as intersectional imbalances (e.g., gender combined with age or skin tone), across the global dataset.

Evaluating the distribution of ICD-10 codes and tracking the informational novelty of dataset releases over time to identify the overrepresentation of common neoplasms and the underrepresentation of rare pathologies.
